> 載營魄抱一，能無離乎？專氣致柔，能嬰兒乎？滌除玄覽，能無疵乎？

Chapter 10 asks six questions and answers none of them. Then it closes with four characters: 玄德.

The six look like six different topics — body and soul, breath, contemplation, governing, the senses, knowledge. They are the same question asked six times: are you acting as the owner?

## 對外做租客，對內做主人

That is the chapter's whole instruction, and it is a division of authority, not a mood.

Toward heaven, earth, and the ten thousand things, you are a tenant. You may cultivate, build, tend, use. You may not own, may not dictate, may not rewrite another thing's own nature. The mistake that produces most of the damage in the world is a tenant acting like a landlord.

Toward your own mind, you are the only one with full authority. No one else can do the work; no one else can be delegated the watching. A tenant there would be an abdication.

## The six questions

1. 載營魄抱一，能無離乎 — can body and spirit hold the one without separating?
2. 專氣致柔，能嬰兒乎 — can you concentrate the breath until it is soft, like an infant's?
3. 滌除玄覽，能無疵乎 — can you cleanse the inner seeing until no flaw remains?
4. 愛民治國，能無為乎 — can you care for people and govern without forcing?
5. 天門開闔，能為雌乎 — when the gates open and close, can you be the receiving side?
6. 明白四達，能無知乎 — with clarity reaching everywhere, can you not-know?

Each is a capacity question, and each is phrased 能…乎 — can you? Not "you should." The chapter is not issuing commands; it is asking you to check.

The sixth is the sharpest. 明白四達 is the state most people are trying to reach: clear, informed, penetrating. The question is whether you can be all that and still not convert clarity into a claim. 無知 here is not ignorance; it is knowing without the knowing becoming a position.

## 玄德

> 生之畜之，生而不有，為而不恃，長而不宰，是謂玄德.

Four clauses, all with the same shape: produce, and don't convert production into ownership; act, and don't lean on the act; let grow, and don't govern the growth.

宰 is the key character — to slaughter, to rule, to be the one who decides what the thing is allowed to become. 不宰 is not neglect. It is the refusal to be the authority over another's nature.

玄德 is not a virtue to acquire. It is what is left when the ownership reflex is absent. The chapter asks six questions, and the answer to all six is the same: stop being the proprietor.

## The asymmetry

The tenant/owner split is not symmetrical, and that is why it works.

Inside, ownership is necessary: someone must decide, watch, and take responsibility, and there is no one else. Outside, ownership is a category error: other people and other things have their own natures, and the attempt to own them produces either resistance or a hollow compliance that looks like agreement and is not.

Most conflict at work and at home is a tenant who has forgotten the lease, negotiating as if the property were his.
